lean.statement:
theorem backward_interpolation_contraction_of_growth
    {interpolation interpolation' : ℝ → ℝ} {rate s t : ℝ}
    (hcontinuous : Continuous interpolation)
    (hderiv : ∀ u : ℝ,
      HasDerivWithinAt interpolation (interpolation' u) (Ici u) u)
    (hgrowth : ∀ u : ℝ,
      rate * interpolation u ≤ interpolation' u)
    (hst : s ≤ t) :
    interpolation s ≤
      interpolation t * Real.exp (-rate * (t - s))
approved_definition_context: HasDerivWithinAt f fPrime (Ici u) u means that f has the supplied one-sided derivative fPrime at u within the right ray [u, infinity).
Continuous interpolation is global continuity on the real line. Real.exp is the real exponential function and is strictly positive.
All functions, parameters, products, inequalities, and endpoint times in the proposition are real-valued.
